scopeNotes.spatial-cross-product: The normal has square-metre components because both input vectors are lengths. Its norm is parallelogram area; the corresponding triangle has half that area. A zero cross product has no distinguished normal direction. The fixed projection is not an area measurement.
scopeNotes.scalar-triple-product: This triangular edge family has signed triple product a b h. Geometric volume is its absolute value. Zero height or a collapsed base gives zero volume even if visible slanted edges remain. The displayed drawing is a fixed projection, not a volume scale.
scopeNotes.coordinate-transformation: This is a passive coordinate change between orthonormal frames. Coordinates transform by the transpose of the frame rotation; the vector itself does not rotate. Angle controls use degrees, converted to radians for trigonometry.
scopeNotes.vector-projection: The reference vector must be nonzero. Multiplying it by a positive factor leaves the projection unchanged, while reversing it reverses the signed scalar component and preserves the projection vector. The residual is orthogonal to the reference; projection is not the full displacement.
scopeNotes.angular-velocity: The exact constant-rate position uses θ=ωt in radians. Speed is nonnegative even when angular velocity is negative. At the centre or at zero rate the rim velocity is zero and has no direction. No force, rolling contact or angular acceleration is modeled.
scopeNotes.linear-momentum: This is Newtonian momentum at the stated instant, not kinetic energy, stopping distance or a collision forecast. Velocity and momentum use separate declared arrow scales because their units differ. A stationary cart has zero momentum and no distinguished momentum direction.
